title: Fault-tolerant request telemetry echo layer for ephemeral runtimes
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Background: We see intermittent loss of tracing context for short-lived worker tasks (ephemeral runtimes, Lambda-style invocations and transient sidecars) which causes broken traces and inflated partial spans in dashboards. This ticket implements a lightweight 'telemetry echo layer' in SDKs and server proxies to ensure request identifiers and minimal provenance propagate across protocols without blocking fast paths.

Goals: 1) Guarantee a stable request and trace identifier for ephemeral contexts across HTTP/gRPC/WS/fifo-worker transports. 2) Provide a non-blocking, low-overhead mechanism to attach fallback provenance when upstream headers are missing. 3) Make instrumentation resilient to partial failures (dropped headers, binary payload truncation) and avoid adding tail latency. 4) Surface enough telemetry for sampling reconciliation and debug traces without inflating storage costs.

Scope: SDK middleware (Node, Python), edge proxy hook, and a small runtime helper library to normalise IDs and emit an 'echo' header when original propagation metadata is absent. This work must integrate with existing sampling hints and the request-fabric components, but avoid synchronous network calls during span creation.

Design decisions to date: - Use header-first approach: prefer standard traceparent/baggage and our legacy X-RW-* headers, falling back to a generated stable-id placed into X-RW-ECHO header for downstream consumption. - Avoid local sync I/O: generation and enrichment use fast in-memory ops and async background flushes for non-critical provenance. - Make serverless-friendly: the echo header includes a 64-bit stable request hash + source fingerprint (service id + timestamp bucket) so downstream can correlate without full parent context. - Sampling reconciliation: include lightweight sampling-hint byte in the echo header so downstream can align with upstream sampling decisions without fetching a control plane.

Trade-offs: - Binary envelope formats (faster, compact) were considered but rejected for broad compatibility with existing edge proxies and to avoid changing wire layers. - We accept some duplication in storage (echoed metadata persisted in some spans) for the benefit of trace completeness in ephemeral workloads. - There is a small increase in header size; we mitigate by compacting the echo payload and rotating the fingerprint epoch to keep values short.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Node and Python) include middleware that attaches X-RW-ECHO when propagation headers are missing
Edge proxy can consume X-RW-ECHO and reconstruct a root trace id for backend services
No synchronous network calls are made during request instrumentation path (benchmarked < 5us median overhead)
End-to-end test demonstrating a full trace across an HTTP frontend -> ephemeral worker -> backend with trace continuity preserved
Dashboards updated: ephemeral-run tracing coverage increases by 40% in acceptance test over baseline
comments: 2025-02-13 Alyssa Chen: Spike complete. Prototype uses 64-bit farmhash + service fingerprint. Impl in node-sdk branch feature/echo-layer. See PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4218
2025-02-18 Mateo Ruiz: Perf bench results attached to PR. Median instrumentation overhead 3.2us for Node middleware, p95 7.4us. Python middleware p50 5.6us. Will optimise encoder for p95.

2025-02-22 Jane Patel (review): Concern about header size in websocket upgrade. Suggested compressing fingerprint and moving timestamp bucket to 4-bit epoch index. Also asked for privacy review regarding stable-id entropy.
2025-02-25 Security review notes: entropy and rotate policy OK if epoch <= 24h; ensure stable-id not user-identifiable. Security requested a short doc and tests — added to links.
2025-03-01 Mateo Ruiz: Implemented compact echo encoding and added async background persist for deep provenance. Added integration test for gRPC streaming case.

2025-03-04 Alyssa Chen: Running canary on staging with edge-proxy enabled. Initial dashboards show trace continuity for batch-worker flows improved from 22% to 68% (staging metric). Monitoring for edge cases continues.
